title: Microservices: boundaries, communication and operational cost

videos.script: Lesson 1 ended with a list of forces. Teams that block each other. One part that needs to scale alone. {{forces}} When one of them is strong enough, a piece of the program moves out and becomes a service. {{split}} A service is not a small program. It is a program that owns a piece of the business and its data, and that can be deployed without asking anybody. {{definition}} The hard part is where to draw the line. Draw it in the wrong place and the two halves talk all day and change together anyway. {{boundary}} In this lesson Quitanda's stock moves out. You will measure what one call across the network costs against a call inside the program. {{measure}} You will stop one service and watch the other cope, or not. {{failure}} And you will see an order go wrong in a way the monolith made impossible. {{inconsistency}} At the end there is a bill: everything a second service adds to build, deploy and watch. Paying it is a decision. This lesson is about making it with the numbers in front of you.
